answer: Orders per customer fell -11.36% (5.44 -> 4.82 trips), and average order value fell -4.48% (KSh 1,694 -> KSh 1,619). Log-mean attribution puts KSh 2.46M of growth on new customers, KSh 5.53M against frequency and KSh 2.10M against basket value.

question: Where is the frequency and basket loss concentrated?
answer: Two of six stores explain 71.3% of the entire group decline: Mombasa Nyali (KSh -2.18M, -27.0%) and Thika Road (KSh -1.50M, -18.7%). Frequency fell -11.7% at Mombasa and -23.7% at Thika Road, versus -11.4% for the group.

question: Why did Mombasa Nyali lose so much more than the rest of the chain?
answer: Its two hero Personal Care SKUs were off the shelf for six weeks: 76 out-of-stock days out of 84 observations (9.5% shelf availability, first gap 2026-08-10). Personal Care revenue at that store fell -34.2% — but Mombasa's average order value also fell -22.6% (KSh 1,724 -> KSh 1,334) against a group AOV change of -4.5%. The missing items cost the whole basket, not just the category.
actionable: Yes — this is a supply-chain event with a date and a store

question: Why were the SKUs unavailable for six weeks?
answer: The data shows WHAT happened (a 40-day gap on the worst single SKU, longest consecutive outage 33 days) but cannot show WHY. Replenishment, supplier and lead-time data are not in this dataset. Candidate causes — single-sourced supply, no safety stock, a mis-set reorder point — are HYPOTHESES and must be labelled as such until procurement data is pulled.
